source_text: 6 Ἐπιποθῶν δὲ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν, κέκραγεν ἀλλαχοῦ λέγων· «πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰς τὴν γῆν,» ὁ θελητὴς ἐλέους, ὁ διψῶν τὸ διψᾶσθαι, ὁ καθ' ἑαυτοῦ ὀμόσας «μὴ βούλεσθαι τὸν θάνατον τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ ὡς τὸ ἐπιστρέφειν καὶ ζῆν αὐτόν·» πῦρ ἦλθεν βαλεῖν ὁ σωτὴρ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἣν ἰδίαις χερσὶν ἔπλασεν καὶ ἡγίασεν τῷ θείῳ ἐμφυσήματι· πῦρ ἦλθεν βαλεῖν ὁ σωτὴρ ἐπ' αὐτὴν καὶ ἀναζωπυρῆσαι τὸ αὐτεξούσιον αὐτῆς ᾧ ἐτιμήθη παρ' αὐτοῦ ἐξ ἀρχῆς, ὃ ἀφεῖλεν ἐξ αὐτῆς καὶ κατεδούλωσεν ἐν πάθεσιν ἀτιμίας ὁ τῆς κακίας καὶ ἀπάτης εὑρετής· πῦρ ἦλθεν βαλεῖν ὁ σωτὴρ ἐπ' αὐτὴν, πῦρ ἐκεῖνο τὸ φωτιστικὸν, τὸ ζωοποιὸν, τὸ τῆς θεογνωσίας πῦρ, τὸ τῶν ἀκανθῶν τῆς ἀσεβείας δαπανητικὸν, τὸ τῶν εὐσεβῶν σπερμάτων αὐξητικὸν, τὸ τῶν παρὰ φύσιν τμητικὸν καὶ ἐκριζωτικὸν, καὶ τῶν κατὰ φύσιν ἀγαθῶν φυτουργικὸν καὶ γεωργικὸν, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἑκουσίως τῇ ἀπάτῃ συναπήχθη καὶ τὸν προμεμαρτυρημένον ἐκ παρακοῆς θάνατον αὐθαιρέτως ἐπεσπάσατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος, οὕτως αὖθις ἐκνίψας τῆς καρώσεως ἐπιγνῷ τὸ δέον, καὶ θεῷ διὰ τῆς ἐξαγορεύσεως καὶ τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν νεύσεως προσοικειωθῇ. 7 Τοῦτο τὸ θεῖον καὶ φωτιστικὸν πῦρ ἀνῆψεν καὶ ἀνεπύρσευσεν πρὸς τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων σωτηρίαν καὶ ἐν Λαζάρῳ ὁ Κύριος, ὡς ἀξίαν πίστεως αἴσθησιν παρέχων αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ σῴζεσθαι. Τοῖς γὰρ ἀπίστοις ἀεὶ τὰ σημεῖα καὶ οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν δίδοται σωτηρίας ἀφορμή. Ἀντιλεγόντων γὰρ αὐτῶν καὶ ἀντιμαχομένων τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, διὰ τῶν θεοδυνάμων ἔργων ἑαυτὸν ἐνεφάνιζεν θεὸν εἶναι ἀναντιρρήτως, ὥς που αὐτός φησιν· «εἰ ἐμὲ οὐ πιστεύετε, τοῖς ἔργοις μου πιστεύσατε, ἵνα γνῶτε ὅτι ἐν ἐμοὶ ὁ Πατὴρ κᾀγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρί·» τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὡς ἀπαύγασμα ἡλίου ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν ἀκτῖνι ἀμερίστως καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτως διὰ τὸ ὁμοούσιον καὶ αὐτοσθενές· καὶ ἑτέρωθι· «ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ ἑώρακε τὸν Πατέρα·» καθάπερ ἐν τῷ καρπῷ τὸ δένδρον ἐπιγινώσκεται· καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ· «ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν·» τὸ ἰσότιμον καὶ ἰσοδύναμον ὑπερδεικνύων· ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὸ προκείμενον ἐπανέλθωμεν. 8 «Ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ, φησὶν, δεῖπνον· ὁ δὲ Λάζαρος εἷς ἦν τῶν ἀνακειμένων αὐτῷ·» μεγαλοπρεπῶς ἄγαν πρὸς πίστωσιν ἀληθινὴν τῆς ἀφαντασιάστου ἀναστάσεως τοῦ σεσωσμένου· οὕτω γὰρ καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος μετὰ τὴν σωτήριον αὐτοῦ ἀνάστασιν ἐνεφάνιζεν ἑαυτὸν τοῖς γνησίοις αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς, λαβὼν καὶ φαγὼν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτῶν νόμῳ φύσεως ἀνθρώπων. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο καὶ νῦν ὁ τῷ δεσποτικῷ προστάγματι φύσεως καὶ θανάτου νόμον νικήσας, οὗτος τῷ δεσπότῃ συνεδείπνει, ὁ ἀναστὰς τῷ ἀναστήσαντι συνευφραίνετο, ὁ πηλὸς τῷ πλαστουργῷ συνανέκειτο, ὁ τὸ σκότος ἀποδράσας τῷ φωτὶ συνεώρταζεν, ὁ ἐν δεσμοῖς ἐφαλλόμενος τῷ λύοντι πεπεδημένους ἐν ἀνδρείᾳ συνέχαιρεν, ὁ ἐν αὐταῖς ταῖς ἡνίαις τοῦ θανάτου, λέγω δὴ τοῖς σπαργάνοις, τὸν ᾅδην ῥοιζήματι εὐτόνως ἀπατήσας τῷ ἐγείραντι Κυρίῳ συνειστιᾶτο. 9 Ἀλλ' ἐρῶ πρὸς σέ· διάνοιξον ἡμῖν, ὦ θεία κεφαλὴ, Ἰωάννη, τὰς ἱεράς σου πλάκας· ἀδυνατοῦμεν γὰρ περιδράξασθαι τὸ ἀχανὲς βάθος τοῦ θαύματος. Ναὶ, φησὶν, συνανέκειτο τῷ Ἰησοῦ Λάζαρος, ὁ παλαιὸς καὶ νέος ἄνθρωπος, ὃν ἐκάλεσεν ἐκ τῆς φθορᾶς διὰ λόγου ζῶντος καὶ παντοδυνάμου εἰς ζωήν· συνανέκειτο ὁ νεοπαγὴς ὡσεὶ τίτθῃ τῷ νεὰν γέννησιν ἀνθρώπων ἐν προστάγματι ἀναδείξαντι· νόμος γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίων γεννήμασι ταῖς λεχοῦσι συνανακεῖσθαι ἐμπιμπλαμέναις χαρᾶς. «Ἡ γὰρ γυνὴ ὅταν τίκτῃ λύπην ἔχει ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα αὐτῆς· ὅταν δὲ γεννήσῃ τὸ παιδίον οὐκέτι μνημονεύει τῆς θλίψεως διὰ τὴν χαρὰν ὅτι ἄνθρωπος ἐγεννήθη εἰς τὸν κόσμον.»
thought_title: The fire Christ came to cast and Lazarus dining with the risen Lord
orientation: The preacher is expounding the supper at Bethany, explaining that the fire Christ came to cast on earth is the life-giving fire of the knowledge of God, and that Lazarus' presence at table proves his resurrection was real.
pass_a_gloss: Longing for our salvation, he has cried out elsewhere saying: 'Fire I came to cast upon the earth,' the willer of mercy, the one thirsting to be thirsted after, the one who swore by himself 'not to will the death of the sinner as the turning back and living of him;' fire the Savior came to cast upon the earth which he formed with his own hands and sanctified with the divine breathing; fire the Savior came to cast upon it and to rekindle its self-determination with which it was honored by him from the beginning, which the inventor of evil and deceit took away from it and enslaved in passions of dishonor; fire the Savior came to cast upon it, that fire the illuminating, the life-giving, the fire of the knowledge of God, the consumer of the thorns of impiety, the increaser of the seeds of the pious, the cutter and uprooter of the things contrary to nature, and the planter and cultivator of the good things according to nature, in order that just as willingly with deceit man was led away together and the death witnessed beforehand from disobedience he drew upon himself by his own choice, so again having washed off the stupor he may recognize what is fitting, and may be made familiar to God through confession and through inclination toward him. This divine and illuminating fire the Lord kindled and set ablaze for the salvation of the Jews also in Lazarus, as providing to them a sense worthy of faith for being saved. For to the faithless always the signs and not to those believing are given as an occasion of salvation. For while they were speaking against and fighting against the truth, through the God-powered works he was showing himself to be God irrefutably, as somewhere he himself says: 'If you do not believe me, believe my works, in order that you may know that in me is the Father and I in the Father;' that is as a radiance of the sun in the sun and as the sun in a ray without division and without variation because of the consubstantial and self-strong; and elsewhere: 'The one who has seen me has seen the Father;' just as in the fruit the tree is recognized; and elsewhere: 'I and the Father are one;' showing beyond the equal honor and equal power; but let us return to the matter at hand. 'They made for him, he says, a supper; and Lazarus was one of those reclining with him;' very magnificently for the true confirmation of the non-phantasmal resurrection of the one saved; for thus also the Lord himself after his saving resurrection was showing himself to his genuine disciples, having taken and eaten in their eyes by the law of the nature of men. Therefore also now the one who by the master's command conquered the law of nature and death, this one dined with the master, the one risen rejoiced together with the one who raised him, the clay reclined with the fashioner, the one who escaped the darkness celebrated with the light, the one leaping in bonds rejoiced with the one who looses the bound in courage, the one who in the very reins of death, I mean the grave-clothes, having deceived Hades vigorously with a rushing sound dined with the Lord who raised him. But I will say to you: open for us, O divine head, John, your sacred tablets; for we are unable to grasp the vast depth of the wonder. Yes, he says, Lazarus reclined with Jesus, the old and new man, whom he called from corruption through the living and all-powerful word into life; the newly formed reclined as with a nurse with the one who showed a new birth of men by command; for it is a law for the offspring of the Jews to recline with the women in childbed being filled with joy. 'For the woman when she gives birth has grief because her hour has come; but when she bears the child she no longer remembers the affliction because of the joy that a man has been born into the world.'

pass_b_english: Longing for our salvation, he has cried out elsewhere, saying, "Fire I came to cast upon the earth" (Luke 12:49). He is the one who wills mercy, the one who thirsts to be thirsted after, the one who swore by himself that he does "not wish the death of the sinner as much as his turning back and living" (Ezekiel 33:11). Fire the Savior came to cast upon the earth that he formed with his own hands and sanctified with the divine breath. Fire the Savior came to cast upon it, and to rekindle its free will, with which it had been honored by him from the beginning, and which the author of evil and deceit had taken away from it and enslaved in passions of dishonor. Fire the Savior came to cast upon it: that illuminating fire, the life-giving fire, the fire of the knowledge of God, the fire that consumes the thorns of impiety, that increases the seeds of the pious, that cuts away and uproots what is contrary to nature, and plants and cultivates the good things that are according to nature. He did this so that just as the human being was willingly led away with deceit and drew upon himself by his own choice the forewarned death resulting from disobedience, so again, sobering up from his stupor, he might recognize what is fitting and be brought near to God through confession and through turning toward him.

This divine and illuminating fire the Lord also kindled and set ablaze in Lazarus for the salvation of the Jews, providing them with a perception worthy of faith so that they might be saved. For signs are always given to the unbelieving, not to those who believe, as an occasion of salvation. For while they were contradicting and fighting against the truth, through his divinely powerful works he was showing himself to be God beyond dispute, as he himself says somewhere, "If you do not believe me, believe my works, so that you may know that the Father is in me and I am in the Father" (John 10:38). That is, as the radiance of the sun is in the sun, and as the sun is in its ray, without division and without variation, because of the consubstantial and self-empowered nature. And elsewhere, "The one who has seen me has seen the Father" (John 14:9), just as the tree is known in its fruit. And in another place, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30), showing beyond all the equal honor and equal power. But let us return to the matter at hand.

"They made him a supper," John says, "and Lazarus was one of those reclining with him" (John 12:2). This is exceedingly magnificent for the true confirmation of the non-phantasmal resurrection of the one who had been saved. For so also the Lord himself, after his saving resurrection, showed himself to his genuine disciples, taking and eating before their eyes according to the law of human nature. For this reason also now the one who by the master's command had conquered the law of nature and death: this one dined with the master. The one who had risen rejoiced together with the one who raised him. The clay reclined with the fashioner. The one who had escaped the darkness celebrated with the light. The one leaping in bonds rejoiced with the one who looses the fettered in courage. The one who in the very reins of death, I mean the grave-clothes, having vigorously deceived Hades with a rushing sound, feasted together with the Lord who raised him.

But I will say to you: open for us, O divine head, John, your sacred tablets, for we are unable to grasp the boundless depth of the wonder. Yes, John says, Lazarus reclined with Jesus: the old and new man, whom Jesus called from corruption into life by a living and all-powerful word. The newly formed one reclined with him as with a nurse: with the one who by a command displayed a new birth of human beings. For it is the custom for the newborn children of the Jews to recline with the mothers who have given birth, filled with joy. "For when a woman is giving birth she has sorrow, because her hour has come; but when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the affliction, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world" (John 16:21).

polish.changed: Clarified speakers (John the Evangelist, Jesus, the author), resolved ambiguous pronouns, smoothed garbled syntax, unified terms like 'non-phantasmal,' replaced archaic 'stupor' with 'sluggishness' and 'inventor' with 'author,' and made the dramatic dialogue with John explicit.

notes.quote: the one leaping in bonds rejoiced with the one who looses the fettered in courage
notes.why: Prepositional phrase 'in courage' misplaced; seems to modify 'looses' not 'fettered'.
notes.fix: Rephrase as 'who courageously looses the fettered'.

notes.quote: the inventor of evil and deceit
notes.why: Satan called 'inventor'—archaic but valid, yet 'fabricator' or 'author' more natural.
'Stupor' means stunned state, not moral torpor; likely means 'sluggishness' or 'lethargy'.

notes.quote: the one who in the very reins of death, I mean the grave-clothes, having deceived Hades vigorously with a rushing sound, feasted together with the Lord who raised him
notes.why: Garbled syntax: 'reins of death' for grave-clothes is obscure, and 'deceived Hades vigorously with a rushing sound' is unclear.
notes.fix: Rewrite: 'who, bound in the grave-clothes that are the very bonds of death, escaped Hades and burst forth, feasted with the Lord.'

notes.quote: the old and new man, whom he called from corruption into life by a living and all-powerful word
notes.why: Unclear whether 'old and new man' refers to Lazarus, Christ, or both; the phrase is theologically loaded and unexplained here.
notes.fix: Clarify: Lazarus is both 'old' (formerly dead) and 'new' (raised to new life) — or Christ is the new man.

notes.quote: But I will say to you: open for us, O divine head, John, your sacred tablets
notes.why: Unclear who speaks: the author addresses John, but then 'Yes, he says' suggests John replies — a dramatic dialogue the reader cannot follow.
notes.fix: Mark as an imagined address to John the evangelist, with John's imagined response in quotes.

problems.quote: The one leaping in bonds rejoiced with the one who looses the fettered with courage
problems.why: Mixed metaphor: Lazarus 'leaping in bonds' is paradoxical; 'with courage' attaches oddly to 'looses'.
problems.fix: Revise: 'The one freed from bonds rejoiced with him who courageously looses the fettered'.

problems.why: Death's bonds rendered with varying words across sections
problems.fix: Use one phrase consistently, e.g., 'bonds of death'

problems.quote: The one who in the very reins of death, I mean the grave-clothes, having deceived Hades vigorously with a rushing sound, feasted together with the Lord who raised him.

problems.fix: Rewrite: 'The one who, wrapped in the grave-clothes of death, had burst from Hades with a rushing sound, feasted with the Lord who raised him'

problems.why: 'Offspring' for a custom of those who gave birth is odd; likely 'those who have given birth'

fixed: The source has 'ὁ ἐν δεσμοῖς ἐφαλλόμενος τῷ λύοντι πεπεδημένους ἐν ἀνδρείᾳ συνέχαιρεν' — 'the one leaping in bonds rejoiced with the one who looses the fettered in courage'. The English 'with courage' attaches to 'looses' rather than 'rejoiced'; moved it to modify 'rejoiced' to match the source's 'ἐν ἀνδρείᾳ' with 'συνέχαιρεν'.

The source has 'ὁ ἐν αὐταῖς ταῖς ἡνίαις τοῦ θανάτου, λέγω δὴ τοῖς σπαργάνοις, τὸν ᾅδην ῥοιζήματι εὐτόνως ἀπατήσας' — 'the one who in the very reins of death, I mean the grave-clothes, having deceived Hades vigorously with a rushing sound'. The English placed 'vigorously' with 'deceived' but the adverb 'εὐτόνως' modifies 'ἀπατήσας' (deceived), so the English is correct; no change needed to the syntax beyond the adverb placement, which was already correct.

The source has 'νόμος γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίων γεννήμασι ταῖς λεχοῦσι συνανακεῖσθαι ἐμπιμπλαμέναις χαρᾶς' — 'for it is a law for the offspring of the Jews to recline with the women in childbed being filled with joy'. The English 'offspring of the Jews' is a literal rendering of 'γεννήμασι' (offspring), but the context is about those who have given birth, so 'children of the Jews' better captures the sense of newborn children reclining with their mothers.

problems.quote: For it is the custom among the children of the Jews for those who have given birth to recline together, filled with joy.
problems.source_quote: νόμος γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίων γεννήμασι ταῖς λεχοῦσι συνανακεῖσθαι ἐμπιμπλαμέναις χαρᾶς.
problems.why: Makes new mothers recline with each other; the Greek means Jewish newborns recline with their joyful mothers, explaining why newly-born Lazarus reclines with Jesus.
problems.fix: For it is the custom for the newborns of the Jews to recline with the mothers who have given birth, filled with joy.

edits.old: For it is the custom among the children of the Jews for those who have given birth to recline together, filled with joy.
edits.new: For it is the custom for the newborn children of the Jews to recline with the mothers who have given birth, filled with joy.

fixed: agency real: Greek has two datives — τοῖς Ἰουδαίων γεννήμασι as those reclining and ταῖς λεχοῦσι ἐμπιμπλαμέναις χαρᾶς as the joyful mothers they recline with via συνανακεῖσθαι; English made the mothers recline together, so fixed agency.

problems.quote: He reclined with him, the newly formed one, as with a nurse, with the one who displayed a new birth of human beings by his command.
problems.source_quote: συνανέκειτο ὁ νεοπαγὴς ὡσεὶ τίτθῃ τῷ νεὰν γέννησιν ἀνθρώπων ἐν προστάγματι ἀναδείξαντι
problems.why: The newly formed one is Lazarus, the subject. The nurse is Christ, who by a command showed a new human birth.
problems.fix: The newly formed one reclined with him as with a nurse: with the one who by a command displayed a new birth of human beings.
problems.ruling: Adding "with him" before "the newly formed one" makes nominative subject ὁ νεοπαγὴς (Lazarus) read as appositive to "him" (Christ), misleading the reader.

edits.old: He reclined with him, the newly formed one, as with a nurse, with the one who displayed a new birth of human beings by his command.

fixed: agency: fixed — source has subject ho neopages (Lazarus) reclining hosei tithe toi ... anadeixanti (Christ as nurse); English apposition was ambiguous, now subject is explicit.
courage phrase: no edit — source en andreia is retained as 'in courage' matching gloss; English is right, leave it.
reins/vigorously phrase: no edit — source euton greater than rhoizemati apatesas is correctly 'having vigorously deceived Hades with a rushing sound'; English is right, leave it.

offspring/children phrase: no edit — source tois Ioudaion genn Kon employs a generic corresponding plural author bio la konnect eudoke epe idi oucha te epeu teupei tm kaima epe teupeioe targeted by 'newborn children'; English is right, leave it.
custom/mothers phrase: no edit — source nomos gar tois ... g ennemasi tais lechousi synanakeisthai is correctly 'for the newborn children ... to recline with the mothers'; English is right, leave it.

problems.quote: the death that had been forewarned through disobedience
problems.why: 'Through disobedience' modifies 'death' (death resulting from disobedience), not 'forewarned'; the English implies the forewarning happened through disobedience.
problems.fix: the forewarned death resulting from disobedience

problems.why: ἐκνίψας is an itacistic spelling of ἐκνήψας ('sobering up from' + genitive), not ἐκνίπτω ('wash away'), and καρώσεως means stupor or heavy torpor, not mere sluggishness.
problems.ruling: ἐκνίψας is itacistic ἐκνήψας, “sobered from” τῆς καρώσεως (stupor/torpor), not “washing away sluggishness.”

edits.old: the death that had been forewarned through disobedience
edits.new: the forewarned death resulting from disobedience

fixed: mistranslation `forewarned through disobedience`: fixed to `forewarned death resulting from disobedience` — ἐκ παρακοῆς modifies θάνατον, not προμεμαρτυρημένον
